features.title: The Planetarium
features.body: Ten spheres of Webb and NASA pictures orbit a sun, drawn live in Metal with HDR light. Tap one to fly to it, unlock it and watch it ignite star by star, then fly inside: the pictures hang all around you, Webb's at their real places in the sky. Tilt your iPhone to look around.

features.title: Curated Webb Gallery
features.body: Webb's greatest images, from the Cosmic Cliffs and the Pillars of Creation to the first deep field, grouped into collections and shown with their real captions, credits, distances and sky coordinates. Search for any target.

features.title: Where Is Webb
features.body: A dashboard for the telescope itself: days in space, its orbit 1.5 million km away at Lagrange Point 2, and the temperatures of its sun-facing side and its shaded instruments.

features.title: Picture of the Day
features.body: NASA's Astronomy Picture of the Day every morning with AI-generated facts that make it make sense, On This Day from up to thirty years back, and a widget for your Home Screen and Lock Screen.

features.title: Asteroid Tracker
features.body: Every close approach of the last four weeks, nearest first, with size, speed and distance in lunar distances, and charts that sort the dangerous from the safe. Always free, never gated.

features.title: Five platforms, one app
features.body: Native on iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple TV and Vision Pro, with Ambient Mode on every screen, a menu bar extra on Mac and Spatial Scenes on Vision Pro. Premium and every sphere unlock on all of them, with Family Sharing.

howItWorks.body: Get Solar Beam free from the App Store on iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple TV or Vision Pro. No account: today's NASA picture, Where Is Webb and the asteroid tracker are always free.
Tap a sphere to fly to it, unlock the ones you love and step inside, or browse the curated Webb gallery with the story behind every picture.
Solar Beam Premium adds the complete Webb gallery, 4K wallpapers, Ambient Mode, the whole archive and unlimited AI facts for $4.99 a month, $19.99 a year or $39.99 once for lifetime access.

faq.q: What makes Solar Beam's James Webb gallery special?
faq.a: It's a curated gallery of the telescope's best images — not a raw data dump. Each image comes with its real caption, credit, distance, instruments, and sky coordinates, grouped into collections (nebulae, galaxies, deep fields, the solar system, and more), and you can search for any target. A "Where Is Webb" dashboard shows the telescope's mission status alongside it.

New in Solar Beam 6.0: ten spheres of pictures orbit a sun, drawn live in Metal. Webb: First Light, Nebulae, Galaxies, Star Birth, Our Solar System and Picture of the Month, which keeps growing. NASA: Hubble Classics, Apollo, Mars, and Saturn & Cassini. Tap one to fly to it; unlock it and it ignites star by star as its pictures arrive, then fly inside and the pictures hang all around you, Webb's at their real places in the sky. With Premium, Your Sky keeps every picture you open on your device and shines at the center. The Planetarium needs iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS or visionOS 26.4 or later.

Solar Beam is a single universal app for iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple TV and Vision Pro, and it's free on all of them. Premium and every Planetarium sphere unlock on every device you own and are family-shareable. It's native on each: a menu bar extra on Mac, Ambient Mode everywhere, the Planetarium around you and Spatial Scenes on Vision Pro.

faq.q: How much does Solar Beam cost?
faq.a: Solar Beam is free to download, and the daily NASA picture, the asteroid tracker and the "Where Is Webb" dashboard are always free. Premium is optional: $4.99 a month, $19.99 a year, or $39.99 once for lifetime access. Subscriptions auto-renew until you cancel in your App Store account; the lifetime unlock never renews. All options are family-shareable and cover every Apple device.

faq.q: What do I get for free versus Premium?
faq.a: Free covers today's picture and the past week, the near-Earth asteroid tracker, the "Where Is Webb" dashboard, the first 24 images of the curated Webb gallery, the Picture of the Day widget and one AI-generated fact set to try. Premium unlocks the complete Webb gallery, 4K wallpapers and full-resolution downloads, Ambient Mode, the full Picture of the Day archive, Spatial Scenes on Vision Pro, unlimited AI facts, the Webb Daily widget and Your Sky. Asteroid tracking is never gated.

Spheres are one-time purchases, separate from Premium: $4.99 each, $6.99 for Picture of the Month, $19.99 for the Webb Collection of six, $14.99 for the NASA Collection of four, or $39.99 for the Complete Planetarium with every sphere released through 2027. Premium members pay 20% less. Each is yours once, shared with your family and kept offline on every Apple device you use.

faq.q: Is there a subscription or in-app purchase?
faq.a: Only if you want more. The app is free. Premium is $4.99 a month or $19.99 a year — both auto-renewing until cancelled — or a $39.99 one-time lifetime unlock that never renews. Manage or cancel anytime in your App Store account. The daily picture and asteroid tracker stay free either way.

faq.q: Where do the images and data come from?
faq.a: From NASA's public APIs and the ESA/Webb archive: the Astronomy Picture of the Day (APOD), James Webb Space Telescope imagery (ESA/Webb, CC BY 4.0), and near-Earth object data. Image credits: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI. Solar Beam is an independent app and is not affiliated with or endorsed by NASA or ESA.

faq.q: Can I really set Webb images as wallpaper?
faq.a: Yes. With Premium, save any Webb image at 4K, in desktop and mobile sizes, and set it as your wallpaper on iPhone, iPad or Mac. Free sharing is at display resolution.

faq.q: What does Solar Beam collect about me?
faq.a: There's no account and no third-party tracking. Your App Store purchases are recorded in Midgar's purchase ledger under a random Midgar ID, not your name or Apple ID, so Premium and your spheres follow you across your devices; Apple's privacy label lists them as linked to you, and they are never used for tracking. The app also sends anonymous usage counts, with no identifier, that Midgar publishes at midgarcorp.cc/open. Nothing you browse or save is kept on Midgar's servers: each request sends only what it needs, such as a date, a page, a collection or a search term you typed. The full policy is linked at the bottom of this page.
Yes, for content you've already viewed. Smart caching keeps recent images available offline and makes launches fast. New daily images, the telescope status, and asteroid updates need a connection.
